import "regexp"

  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, timeEnd: time(v: r.end_epoch * 1000000000), text: "Loss incident, " + r.class + " (" + r.confidence + " confidence, " + string(v: r.minutes) + " min): " + r.summary, tags: "incident," + r.class}))

panels.title: ${target} – what is measured, over the selected range
Time since the last measurement
panels.description: How long ago any probe of this target (ICMP, TCP, HTTP or DNS) last wrote a point inside the selected range, and when that point is. Relative to now: green within 11 minutes (two steps at the default 5-minute step), orange within a day, red beyond. Red means the tiles beside it describe the past, not the present; a range that ends in the past is always red. "no data in this range": nothing from this target in the range at all.

panels.description: Whether this target wrote a point in the last 24 hours, whatever the selected range. When it did not: when it stopped, and, for a retired Netflix appliance name, which slot (Netflix_<slot>_<site>) measures the appliances now: the slots keep their names while the appliance behind each changes daily (target_host records which). The newest point is looked for in the range and the 30 days before it. Click the text to open the slot, or the Netflix side-by-side.

targets.query:
import "array"
import "date"
import "regexp"
import "strings"
// Any name a link brings (Google, Google_h2, cloudflare) selects the whole target:
// drop the probe suffix, then match every probe of that base name, any case.
base = regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: "${target}", t: "")
re = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)?$")
// The newest point of this target up to now (not the range's end: a past range
// must not read as "stopped"), reaching 30 days back from the range start so a
// target that stopped before the range still says when.
newest = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 30d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: now())
  |> filter(fn:(r)=> (r._measurement == "latency" or r._measurement == "tcp_latency" or r._measurement == "http_latency" or r._measurement == "dns_latency") and r.target =~ re and r._field == "loss")
  |> last() |> keep(columns:["_time","category"]) |> group() |> sort(columns:["_time"], desc:true) |> limit(n:1)
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
// The Netflix slots keep their names while the appliance behind each changes daily
// (target_host records which). A retired appliance name ends in its slot number:
// the live slot carrying that number is where its measurements continue.
slot = regexp.findString(r: /_[0-9]+$/, v: base)
slotRe = regexp.compile(v: if slot == "" then "^$" else "^[A-Za-z]+" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: slot) + "_")
live = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:-24h)
  |> filter(fn:(r)=> r._measurement == "latency" and r.category == "netflix" and r._field == "loss" and r.target =~ slotRe)
  |> last() |> keep(columns:["target"]) |> group() |> limit(n:1)
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
since = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:-1y)
  |> filter(fn:(r)=> r._measurement == "target_host" and r._field == "host" and r.category == "netflix" and r.target =~ slotRe)
  |> first() |> keep(columns:["_time","target"]) |> group() |> sort(columns:["_time"]) |> limit(n:1)
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
when = if exists newest._time then strings.replace(v: strings.substring(v: string(v: newest._time), start: 0, end: 16), t: "T", u: " ", i: 1) + " UTC" else ""
category = if exists newest.category then newest.category else ""
slotName = if exists live.target and exists since._time and category == "netflix" then live.target else ""
sinceDay = if exists since._time then strings.substring(v: string(v: since._time), start: 0, end: 10) else ""
stale = not exists newest._time or int(v: now()) - int(v: newest._time) >= 86400000000000
array.from(rows: [{
  _time: now(),
  // The data link opens the slot; for a target without one it opens this target again.
  slot: if slotName != "" then slotName else base,
  _value: if not exists newest._time then "no data: nothing from this target in the range nor in the 30 days before it"
    else if not stale then "measured in the last 24 h: newest point " + when
    else if slotName != "" then "stopped " + when + " · retired name: its slot is measured as " + slotName + " since " + sinceDay
    else if category == "netflix" then "stopped " + when + " · retired name: the Netflix appliances are measured as the Netflix_<slot>_<site> targets"
    else "stopped " + when + " · nothing measured since (removed from the targets, or its probe stopped)"}])
  |> keep(columns:["_time","_value","slot"])

panels.title: Monitor deaf in range
panels.description: Minutes inside the range in which this Pi's own radio heard nothing: Wi-Fi samples in which the uplink's received-packet counter did not move, or the radio was not associated (the definition the alerter, the doctor and the inference module use). Each deaf sample counts the time since the one before it, 10 s by default. Loss in those minutes is the monitor's, not any destination's: subtract it before reading the loss tiles. "none": no deaf sample in the range, or no Wi-Fi uplink (a wired Pi). The "Monitor deaf" and "Loss incidents" annotations mark the spans on the charts; a Monitor deaf span can be longer than these minutes, since the inference period around a short hang covers the clean bins beside it. It reads every Wi-Fi sample in the range (8 640 a day at the default 10 s), so a range of months takes a while to load.

panels.title: Service
panels.description: What this target measures. Value: its service name (docs/taxonomy.md), the label config-manager resolves from the rules, or the override set for this install; the small text over it: its service categories. Not the probe bucket (topsites, netflix...). "unknown (no rule yet)": no rule says yet, not a broken target; the name is then the target's title. As the exporter last recorded it; "no label yet": it has not written one (ClickHouse mode, or the first minutes after an upgrade). Who delivers it is the next tile. The stat reduces over every field (/.*/) on purpose: the string frame is named by its _field label, so a pattern on _value or Value matches nothing and the tile shows its noValue text.

panels.title: Delivered by
panels.description: Who delivers this target: the network its host answers from (its origin AS, from the routing table on the Pi; docs/taxonomy.md, Delivery). Value: that network's operator; the small text over it: its kind (CDN, content network, embedded cache, cloud origin, access network, transit, DNS infrastructure, academic network, local network, other network). "network not identified": no IPv4 answer or no AS lookup yet, not an error; "not looked up yet": a label written before the delivery axis existed. As the exporter last recorded it; "no label yet": it has not written one. Reduces over every field (/.*/), as the Service tile.

panels.title: ICMP
panels.description: Ping (FPing): the network path, no application. "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: TCP handshake
panels.description: SYN / SYN-ACK to port 443: the transport floor under HTTP. "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: HTTP
panels.description: A HEAD request over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (connect + TLS + request + response headers, minus DNS). "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: DNS
panels.description: A DNS query answered by this target, when it is a resolver. "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: ICMP – ${target} – latency (ms)
panels.description: Ping (FPing): the network path, no application. Line: median; shade: 10th–90th percentile; both of every ping in each point's window (one 5-minute cycle on a short range, many on a long one).

panels.title: ICMP – ${target} – loss (%)
panels.description: Share of the cycle's probes that got no answer.

panels.title: TCP handshake – ${target} – latency (ms)
panels.description: SYN / SYN-ACK to port 443: the transport floor under HTTP. Line: median; shade: 10th–90th percentile; both of every ping in each point's window (one 5-minute cycle on a short range, many on a long one).

panels.title: TCP handshake – ${target} – loss (%)
panels.description: Share of the cycle's probes that got no answer.

panels.title: HTTP – ${target} – fetch time by version, median (ms)
panels.description: A HEAD request over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (connect + TLS + request + response headers, minus DNS). One line per version; a downgraded fetch counts as a failure, not as the lower version. Each line is the median of every fetch of that version in the point's window.

panels.title: HTTP – ${target} – failed fetches (%)
panels.description: Fetches that failed or did not use the version they were asked to.

panels.title: DNS – ${target} – latency (ms)
panels.description: A DNS query answered by this target, when it is a resolver. Line: median; shade: 10th–90th percentile; both of every ping in each point's window (one 5-minute cycle on a short range, many on a long one).

defaults.noValue: no DNS data for this target in this range: resolvers are targets of their own (for example GoogleDNS)

panels.title: DNS – ${target} – loss (%)
panels.description: Share of the cycle's probes that got no answer.

defaults.noValue: no DNS data for this target in this range: resolvers are targets of their own (for example GoogleDNS)

panels.title: Path – ${target} – last trace in range (experimental)
panels.description: EXPERIMENTAL. A Paris traceroute (ICMP) once an hour from the path meter. A router's reply time is its slow path's and rate-limited: read it as a description, not as that hop's latency. A change is counted after two traces in a row show it. See docs/path.md. Hops that did not answer are left out of the table; a private hop has no AS. AS from CAIDA's RouteViews prefix-to-AS table; a router on an exchange point's LAN (not announced) is named by its exchange, from PeeringDB. The name (PTR) is the reverse DNS name the operator gave the address: often a hint of where the router is, sometimes stale; it never counts toward a path change. Each row takes its AS's color, so a run of hops in one network reads as one block; the color comes from the AS number (modulo 12), so an AS keeps it on every target, and two networks can share one. Gray: a private, CGNAT, IPv4 loopback, link-local or ULA address, or a hop with no AS (an exchange port without one included).

defaults.noValue: No path: the path meter is off (smoking-pi enable pathmeter), or it has not traced this target in the selected range.

panels.title: Path – ${target} – hop reply time, calm vs hot (experimental)
panels.description: Where on the path the end-to-end RTT rose: each hop's reply time when the target was calm and when it was hot, p10/p50/p90 and the number of traces. Step = hot p50 − calm p50. Persists downstream: the hop holds at least half of the end-to-end step and so does every later hop with hot replies; "starts here" marks the first such hop. A hop needs three hot and three calm traces to be judged. A second address at a later TTL (a route variant or load balancing) that answered fast in three hot traces also counts, and can turn the hops before it to no: read the rows around. Hot and calm come from this target's own end-to-end ICMP RTT (SmokePing's median) in the step that holds each trace, against its baseline, the median of the selected range: hot at least 1.5 times the baseline and 20 ms above it, calm within 10 % and 5 ms of it; traces in between are left out. Not from the Jitterbug periods (the annotation), which can miss a hump. A router's reply time is its own slow path answering a probe that expired there, rate-limited, plus a return path that may not be the forward one: a rise at one hop says nothing by itself. Only a step that persists at every later hop, through to the destination, locates congestion, and even then the direction (to the destination or back) is unknown. EXPERIMENTAL. From the hourly Paris traceroute (one probe per hop); the rounds a loss episode adds are left out, as they land almost only in hot steps. n is the number of hourly traces the hop answered in. Hops are keyed by address and named by their usual TTL (average, rounded), address and AS or exchange; a route variant is another row with few traces. The shared first hops take the fastest reply of the destinations traced from hop 1 in the same cycle. See docs/path.md.

targets.query:
import "internal/debug"
import "join"
import "array"
import "regexp"
import "strings"
import "date"
import "math"
// pathmeter stores one path per base name (docs/path.md): match that name, any case.
base = regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: "${target}", t: "")
re = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "$")
// Its ICMP probe: the base name, or base_icmp where the target has other probes.
icmp = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "(_icmp)?$")
// join refuses an empty side (the path meter off, an empty range): each side gets
// one placeholder row that matches nothing real.
pad = (tables=<-, row) => union(tables: [tables, array.from(rows: [row])])
// The end-to-end ICMP RTT (ms), one point per SmokePing step. Only one of base and
// base_icmp exists for a target: an ICMP-only target has no suffix.
e2e = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r.target =~ icmp and r._field == "median")
  |> group() |> sort(columns: ["_time"]) |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, e2e: float(v: r._value) * 1000.0}))
// The probe's step (60 s to an hour, set per probe): the median spacing of its points.
gap = e2e |> elapsed(unit: 1s) |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with elapsed: float(v: r.elapsed)}))
  |> median(column: "elapsed") |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
stepNs = (if exists gap.elapsed then int(v: gap.elapsed) else 300) * 1000000000
// Hot and calm, relative to this target's own baseline: the range's median RTT
// (the calm level as long as the target was congested less than half the range).
// Hot: at least 1.5 times the baseline and 20 ms above it; calm: within 10 % and
// 5 ms of it. Steps in between are neither, and their traces are left out.
mid = e2e |> median(column: "e2e") |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
baseline = if exists mid.e2e then mid.e2e else 0.0
hotMs = if baseline * 1.5 > baseline + 20.0 then baseline * 1.5 else baseline + 20.0
calmMs = if baseline * 1.1 > baseline + 5.0 then baseline * 1.1 else baseline + 5.0
steps = e2e
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, e2e: r.e2e,
      state: if r.e2e >= hotMs then "hot" else if r.e2e <= calmMs then "calm" else "edge"}))
// This target's hops, from the hourly traces only: the rounds a loss episode adds
// land almost all in hot steps and would weigh one episode many times. The shared
// first hops (TTLs below first_hop) come with the address only: the prefix is the
// same routers at the same TTLs for every target of a cycle, so their reply is the
// fastest of the destinations traced from hop 1 in that cycle at that TTL (the
// least delayed slow path), read for those TTLs only.
hops = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_hop" and r.target =~ re
      and (r._field == "addr" or r._field == "rtt_ms" or r._field == "asn" or r._field == "as_name" or r._field == "ixp"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "ttl"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
first = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_trace" and r.target =~ re and r._field == "first_hop")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> group() |> max() |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
fh = if exists first._value then (if first._value > 10 then 10 else int(v: first._value)) else 1
prefix = if fh > 1 then regexp.compile(v: "^0[1-" + string(v: fh - 1) + "]$") else /^$/
// One row shape for every union below (a union needs the same columns on each side).
hopRow = (r, kind) => ({_time: r._time, ttl: r.ttl, addr: r.addr, kind: kind,
    rtt_ms: if exists r.rtt_ms then float(v: r.rtt_ms) else debug.null(type: "float"),
    asn: if exists r.asn then int(v: r.asn) else debug.null(type: "int"),
    as_name: if exists r.as_name then string(v: r.as_name) else debug.null(type: "string"),
    ixp: if exists r.ixp then string(v: r.ixp) else debug.null(type: "string")})
// Fill instead of join (a join with a predicate compares every pair): one table
// sorted by key, each row taking the value of the row before it, kept only when
// that value came from the same key. Donors sort by their reply, slowest first, so
// the fastest is the one a hop takes.
donors = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_hop" and r._field == "rtt_ms" and r.ttl =~ prefix)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, ttl: r.ttl, addr: debug.null(type: "string"), kind: 0, rtt_ms: float(v: r._value),
      ord: -1.0 * float(v: r._value), key: string(v: r._time) + r.ttl, from: string(v: r._time) + r.ttl,
      asn: debug.null(type: "int"), as_name: debug.null(type: "string"), ixp: debug.null(type: "string")}))
shared = union(tables: [donors, hops |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.rtt_ms)
    |> map(fn: (r) => hopRow(r: r, kind: 1))
    |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ord: 1000000000000.0, key: string(v: r._time) + r.ttl, from: debug.null(type: "string")}))])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time", "ttl", "ord"])
  |> fill(column: "rtt_ms", usePrevious: true) |> fill(column: "from", usePrevious: true)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.kind == 1 and exists r.rtt_ms and r.from == r.key)
  |> drop(columns: ["key", "from", "ord"])
// Each trace takes the state of the SmokePing step that holds it: the first step
// stamped at or after the trace (a step's point closes it), within one step.
// Sorted newest first, so filling from the row before is filling from later.
holding = (tables=<-) => union(tables: [
    steps |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, kind: 2, ttl: "", ttln: 0, addr: debug.null(type: "string"),
        rtt_ms: debug.null(type: "float"), asn: debug.null(type: "int"), as_name: debug.null(type: "string"),
        ixp: debug.null(type: "string"), e2e: r.e2e, state: r.state, from: r._time})),
    tables])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time", "kind"], desc: true)
  |> fill(column: "state", usePrevious: true) |> fill(column: "e2e", usePrevious: true) |> fill(column: "from", usePrevious: true)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.kind == 1 and exists r.from and int(v: r.from) - int(v: r._time) < stepNs)
samples = union(tables: [hops |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.rtt_ms) |> map(fn: (r) => hopRow(r: r, kind: 1)), shared])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ttln: int(v: r.ttl), e2e: debug.null(type: "float"), state: debug.null(type: "string"),
      from: debug.null(type: "time")}))
  |> holding()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.addr)
// RFC 1918, CGNAT 100.64/10, IPv4 loopback, link-local, ULA: as in "Last trace in range".
private = /^(10\.|127\.|169\.254\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\.|(?i)f[cd]|(?i)fe[89ab])/
// One pass over the samples (Flux reads a stream again for every use). Per address
// and state, each reply's rank from both ends gives the count n (the hourly traces
// it answered in) and the p10, p50
// and p90 replies by nearest rank; one reduce per address then gathers both states
// and the hop's name: its usual TTL (the average, rounded), address and AS or exchange.
at = (p, n) => {
    k = int(v: math.ceil(x: p * float(v: n)))
    return if k < 1 then 1 else k
}
stats = samples |> filter(fn: (r) => r.state == "hot" or r.state == "calm")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({addr: r.addr, state: r.state, rtt_ms: r.rtt_ms, ttln: r.ttln, i: 1, j: 1,
      who: if exists r.ixp and r.ixp != "" then "IXP " + r.ixp
           else if exists r.as_name and r.as_name != "" and exists r.asn
             and strings.split(v: r.as_name, t: " - ")[0] != "AS" + string(v: r.asn)
             then "AS" + string(v: r.asn) + " " + strings.split(v: r.as_name, t: " - ")[0]
           else if exists r.asn and r.asn != 0 then "AS" + string(v: r.asn) else ""}))
  |> group(columns: ["addr", "state"]) |> sort(columns: ["rtt_ms"]) |> cumulativeSum(columns: ["i"])
  |> sort(columns: ["i"], desc: true) |> cumulativeSum(columns: ["j"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with n: r.i + r.j - 1}))
  |> group(columns: ["addr"])
  |> reduce(identity: {calm_n: 0, calm_p10: -1.0, calm_p50: -1.0, calm_p90: -1.0,
                       hot_n: 0, hot_p10: -1.0, hot_p50: -1.0, hot_p90: -1.0, seen: 0, ttls: 0, who: ""},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        calm_n: if r.state == "calm" then r.n else accumulator.calm_n,
        calm_p10: if r.state == "calm" and r.i == at(p: 0.1, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.calm_p10,
        calm_p50: if r.state == "calm" and r.i == at(p: 0.5, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.calm_p50,
        calm_p90: if r.state == "calm" and r.i == at(p: 0.9, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.calm_p90,
        hot_n: if r.state == "hot" then r.n else accumulator.hot_n,
        hot_p10: if r.state == "hot" and r.i == at(p: 0.1, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.hot_p10,
        hot_p50: if r.state == "hot" and r.i == at(p: 0.5, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.hot_p50,
        hot_p90: if r.state == "hot" and r.i == at(p: 0.9, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.hot_p90,
        seen: accumulator.seen + 1, ttls: accumulator.ttls + r.ttln,
        who: if accumulator.who != "" then accumulator.who else r.who}))
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ttl: (r.ttls + r.seen / 2) / r.seen}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with hop: (if r.ttl < 10 then "0" else "") + string(v: r.ttl) + " · " + r.addr
      + (if r.who != "" then " · " + r.who
         else if regexp.matchRegexpString(r: private, v: r.addr) then " · private" else " · no AS")}))
// The end-to-end step: what a hop has to carry to count (half of it at least).
eHot = steps |> filter(fn: (r) => r.state == "hot") |> median(column: "e2e") |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
eCalm = steps |> filter(fn: (r) => r.state == "calm") |> median(column: "e2e") |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
e2eStep = if exists eHot.e2e and exists eCalm.e2e then eHot.e2e - eCalm.e2e else 0.0
stats
  // Three traces at least on each side before a hop is judged.
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with hasHot: r.hot_n >= 3 and r.calm_n >= 3, step: r.hot_p50 - r.calm_p50}))
  // A hop carries the step when it holds at least half of the end-to-end step; it
  // persists when it and every later hop with hot replies carry it.
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with carries: r.hasHot and e2eStep > 0.0 and r.step >= e2eStep / 2.0}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with brk: if r.hasHot and not r.carries then 1 else 0}))
  |> sort(columns: ["ttl", "addr"], desc: true) |> cumulativeSum(columns: ["brk"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with persists: if not r.hasHot then (if r.hot_n == 0 then "no hot traces"
      else if r.calm_n == 0 then "no calm traces" else "too few traces (< 3)")
      else if r.carries and r.brk == 0 then "yes" else "no", first: if r.carries and r.brk == 0 then 1 else 0}))
  |> sort(columns: ["ttl", "addr"]) |> cumulativeSum(columns: ["first"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({hop: r.hop, ttl: r.ttl,
      calm_n: r.calm_n, calm_p10: if r.calm_n > 0 then r.calm_p10 else debug.null(type: "float"),
      calm_p50: if r.calm_n > 0 then r.calm_p50 else debug.null(type: "float"), calm_p90: if r.calm_n > 0 then r.calm_p90 else debug.null(type: "float"),
      hot_n: r.hot_n, hot_p10: if r.hot_n > 0 then r.hot_p10 else debug.null(type: "float"),
      hot_p50: if r.hot_n > 0 then r.hot_p50 else debug.null(type: "float"), hot_p90: if r.hot_n > 0 then r.hot_p90 else debug.null(type: "float"),
      step: if r.hot_n > 0 and r.calm_n > 0 then r.step else debug.null(type: "float"),
      persists: if r.persists == "yes" and r.first == 1 then "yes, starts here" else r.persists}))
  |> drop(columns: ["ttl"])

defaults.noValue: No path: the path meter is off (smoking-pi enable pathmeter), it has not traced this target in the selected range, or the target has no ICMP series to tell hot from calm.

panels.title: Path – ${target} – hop reply time minus its calm median, per trace (experimental)
panels.description: Each trace (column) and hop (row): the hop's reply time minus its own calm median, in ms. The last row is the end-to-end RTT at that trace minus the baseline, so a step that starts at one hop and stays red down to it is where the RTT rose. Blank: the hop did not answer, or that trace took another route. Only addresses that answered in at least a tenth of the range's hourly traces (counting the hot and calm ones; three at least) get a row (the table lists them all). Hot and calm come from this target's own end-to-end ICMP RTT (SmokePing's median) in the step that holds each trace, against its baseline, the median of the selected range: hot at least 1.5 times the baseline and 20 ms above it, calm within 10 % and 5 ms of it; traces in between are left out. Not from the Jitterbug periods (the annotation), which can miss a hump. A router's reply time is its own slow path answering a probe that expired there, rate-limited, plus a return path that may not be the forward one: a rise at one hop says nothing by itself. Only a step that persists at every later hop, through to the destination, locates congestion, and even then the direction (to the destination or back) is unknown. EXPERIMENTAL. From the hourly Paris traceroute (one probe per hop); the rounds a loss episode adds are left out, as they land almost only in hot steps. n is the number of hourly traces the hop answered in. Hops are keyed by address and named by their usual TTL (average, rounded), address and AS or exchange; a route variant is another row with few traces. The shared first hops take the fastest reply of the destinations traced from hop 1 in the same cycle. See docs/path.md.

targets.query:
import "internal/debug"
import "join"
import "array"
import "regexp"
import "strings"
import "date"
import "math"
// pathmeter stores one path per base name (docs/path.md): match that name, any case.
base = regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: "${target}", t: "")
re = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "$")
// Its ICMP probe: the base name, or base_icmp where the target has other probes.
icmp = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "(_icmp)?$")
// join refuses an empty side (the path meter off, an empty range): each side gets
// one placeholder row that matches nothing real.
pad = (tables=<-, row) => union(tables: [tables, array.from(rows: [row])])
// The end-to-end ICMP RTT (ms), one point per SmokePing step. Only one of base and
// base_icmp exists for a target: an ICMP-only target has no suffix.
e2e = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r.target =~ icmp and r._field == "median")
  |> group() |> sort(columns: ["_time"]) |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, e2e: float(v: r._value) * 1000.0}))
// The probe's step (60 s to an hour, set per probe): the median spacing of its points.
gap = e2e |> elapsed(unit: 1s) |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with elapsed: float(v: r.elapsed)}))
  |> median(column: "elapsed") |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
stepNs = (if exists gap.elapsed then int(v: gap.elapsed) else 300) * 1000000000
// Hot and calm, relative to this target's own baseline: the range's median RTT
// (the calm level as long as the target was congested less than half the range).
// Hot: at least 1.5 times the baseline and 20 ms above it; calm: within 10 % and
// 5 ms of it. Steps in between are neither, and their traces are left out.
mid = e2e |> median(column: "e2e") |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
baseline = if exists mid.e2e then mid.e2e else 0.0
hotMs = if baseline * 1.5 > baseline + 20.0 then baseline * 1.5 else baseline + 20.0
calmMs = if baseline * 1.1 > baseline + 5.0 then baseline * 1.1 else baseline + 5.0
steps = e2e
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, e2e: r.e2e,
      state: if r.e2e >= hotMs then "hot" else if r.e2e <= calmMs then "calm" else "edge"}))
// This target's hops, from the hourly traces only: the rounds a loss episode adds
// land almost all in hot steps and would weigh one episode many times. The shared
// first hops (TTLs below first_hop) come with the address only: the prefix is the
// same routers at the same TTLs for every target of a cycle, so their reply is the
// fastest of the destinations traced from hop 1 in that cycle at that TTL (the
// least delayed slow path), read for those TTLs only.
hops = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_hop" and r.target =~ re
      and (r._field == "addr" or r._field == "rtt_ms" or r._field == "asn" or r._field == "as_name" or r._field == "ixp"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "ttl"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
first = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_trace" and r.target =~ re and r._field == "first_hop")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> group() |> max() |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
fh = if exists first._value then (if first._value > 10 then 10 else int(v: first._value)) else 1
prefix = if fh > 1 then regexp.compile(v: "^0[1-" + string(v: fh - 1) + "]$") else /^$/
// One row shape for every union below (a union needs the same columns on each side).
hopRow = (r, kind) => ({_time: r._time, ttl: r.ttl, addr: r.addr, kind: kind,
    rtt_ms: if exists r.rtt_ms then float(v: r.rtt_ms) else debug.null(type: "float"),
    asn: if exists r.asn then int(v: r.asn) else debug.null(type: "int"),
    as_name: if exists r.as_name then string(v: r.as_name) else debug.null(type: "string"),
    ixp: if exists r.ixp then string(v: r.ixp) else debug.null(type: "string")})
// Fill instead of join (a join with a predicate compares every pair): one table
// sorted by key, each row taking the value of the row before it, kept only when
// that value came from the same key. Donors sort by their reply, slowest first, so
// the fastest is the one a hop takes.
donors = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_hop" and r._field == "rtt_ms" and r.ttl =~ prefix)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, ttl: r.ttl, addr: debug.null(type: "string"), kind: 0, rtt_ms: float(v: r._value),
      ord: -1.0 * float(v: r._value), key: string(v: r._time) + r.ttl, from: string(v: r._time) + r.ttl,
      asn: debug.null(type: "int"), as_name: debug.null(type: "string"), ixp: debug.null(type: "string")}))
shared = union(tables: [donors, hops |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.rtt_ms)
    |> map(fn: (r) => hopRow(r: r, kind: 1))
    |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ord: 1000000000000.0, key: string(v: r._time) + r.ttl, from: debug.null(type: "string")}))])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time", "ttl", "ord"])
  |> fill(column: "rtt_ms", usePrevious: true) |> fill(column: "from", usePrevious: true)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.kind == 1 and exists r.rtt_ms and r.from == r.key)
  |> drop(columns: ["key", "from", "ord"])
// Each trace takes the state of the SmokePing step that holds it: the first step
// stamped at or after the trace (a step's point closes it), within one step.
// Sorted newest first, so filling from the row before is filling from later.
holding = (tables=<-) => union(tables: [
    steps |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, kind: 2, ttl: "", ttln: 0, addr: debug.null(type: "string"),
        rtt_ms: debug.null(type: "float"), asn: debug.null(type: "int"), as_name: debug.null(type: "string"),
        ixp: debug.null(type: "string"), e2e: r.e2e, state: r.state, from: r._time})),
    tables])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time", "kind"], desc: true)
  |> fill(column: "state", usePrevious: true) |> fill(column: "e2e", usePrevious: true) |> fill(column: "from", usePrevious: true)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.kind == 1 and exists r.from and int(v: r.from) - int(v: r._time) < stepNs)
samples = union(tables: [hops |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.rtt_ms) |> map(fn: (r) => hopRow(r: r, kind: 1)), shared])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ttln: int(v: r.ttl), e2e: debug.null(type: "float"), state: debug.null(type: "string"),
      from: debug.null(type: "time")}))
  |> holding()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.addr)
// RFC 1918, CGNAT 100.64/10, IPv4 loopback, link-local, ULA: as in "Last trace in range".
private = /^(10\.|127\.|169\.254\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\.|(?i)f[cd]|(?i)fe[89ab])/
// One pass over the samples (Flux reads a stream again for every use). Per address
// and state, each reply's rank from both ends gives the count n (the hourly traces
// it answered in) and the p10, p50
// and p90 replies by nearest rank; one reduce per address then gathers both states
// and the hop's name: its usual TTL (the average, rounded), address and AS or exchange.
at = (p, n) => {
    k = int(v: math.ceil(x: p * float(v: n)))
    return if k < 1 then 1 else k
}
stats = samples |> filter(fn: (r) => r.state == "hot" or r.state == "calm")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({addr: r.addr, state: r.state, rtt_ms: r.rtt_ms, ttln: r.ttln, i: 1, j: 1,
      who: if exists r.ixp and r.ixp != "" then "IXP " + r.ixp
           else if exists r.as_name and r.as_name != "" and exists r.asn
             and strings.split(v: r.as_name, t: " - ")[0] != "AS" + string(v: r.asn)
             then "AS" + string(v: r.asn) + " " + strings.split(v: r.as_name, t: " - ")[0]
           else if exists r.asn and r.asn != 0 then "AS" + string(v: r.asn) else ""}))
  |> group(columns: ["addr", "state"]) |> sort(columns: ["rtt_ms"]) |> cumulativeSum(columns: ["i"])
  |> sort(columns: ["i"], desc: true) |> cumulativeSum(columns: ["j"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with n: r.i + r.j - 1}))
  |> group(columns: ["addr"])
  |> reduce(identity: {calm_n: 0, calm_p10: -1.0, calm_p50: -1.0, calm_p90: -1.0,
                       hot_n: 0, hot_p10: -1.0, hot_p50: -1.0, hot_p90: -1.0, seen: 0, ttls: 0, who: ""},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        calm_n: if r.state == "calm" then r.n else accumulator.calm_n,
        calm_p10: if r.state == "calm" and r.i == at(p: 0.1, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.calm_p10,
        calm_p50: if r.state == "calm" and r.i == at(p: 0.5, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.calm_p50,
        calm_p90: if r.state == "calm" and r.i == at(p: 0.9, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.calm_p90,
        hot_n: if r.state == "hot" then r.n else accumulator.hot_n,
        hot_p10: if r.state == "hot" and r.i == at(p: 0.1, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.hot_p10,
        hot_p50: if r.state == "hot" and r.i == at(p: 0.5, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.hot_p50,
        hot_p90: if r.state == "hot" and r.i == at(p: 0.9, n: r.n) then r.rtt_ms else accumulator.hot_p90,
        seen: accumulator.seen + 1, ttls: accumulator.ttls + r.ttln,
        who: if accumulator.who != "" then accumulator.who else r.who}))
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ttl: (r.ttls + r.seen / 2) / r.seen}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with hop: (if r.ttl < 10 then "0" else "") + string(v: r.ttl) + " · " + r.addr
      + (if r.who != "" then " · " + r.who
         else if regexp.matchRegexpString(r: private, v: r.addr) then " · private" else " · no AS")}))
// Every reply minus its hop's calm median; the end-to-end RTT at each trace minus
// the baseline as the last row. Only addresses that answered in at least a tenth of
// the hourly traces (three at least), counting the hot and calm ones, get a row:
// a load-balanced network can answer from dozens.
nTraces = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_trace" and r.target =~ re and r._field == "hops")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> group() |> count() |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
minSeen = if exists nTraces._value and nTraces._value / 10 > 3 then nTraces._value / 10 else 3
deltas = join.inner(
    left: samples |> keep(columns: ["_time", "addr", "rtt_ms"]) |> pad(row: {_time: time(v: 0), addr: "", rtt_ms: 0.0}),
    right: stats |> filter(fn: (r) => r.calm_n > 0 and r.seen >= minSeen) |> keep(columns: ["addr", "hop", "calm_p50"])
      |> pad(row: {addr: "", hop: "", calm_p50: 0.0}),
    on: (l, r) => l.addr == r.addr, as: (l, r) => ({_time: l._time, hop: r.hop, _value: l.rtt_ms - r.calm_p50}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.hop != "")
endToEnd = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_trace" and r.target =~ re and r._field == "hops")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.trigger)
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, kind: 1, ttl: "", ttln: 0, addr: "", rtt_ms: debug.null(type: "float"),
      asn: debug.null(type: "int"), as_name: debug.null(type: "string"), ixp: debug.null(type: "string"),
      e2e: debug.null(type: "float"), state: debug.null(type: "string"), from: debug.null(type: "time")}))
  |> holding()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, hop: "end to end (SmokePing) − baseline", _value: r.e2e - baseline}))
// With nothing else to show, a null point at the range's end: the panel still gets
// a time field (an empty frame is an error to it), and its row says why.
why = if not exists first._value then "no trace in range (path meter off?)"
  else if baseline == 0.0 then "no ICMP series: no hot or calm"
  else "end to end (SmokePing) − baseline"
anchor = array.from(rows: [{_time: v.timeRangeStop, hop: why, _value: 0.0}])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, hop: r.hop, _value: debug.null(type: "float")}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.hop != "end to end (SmokePing) − baseline")
union(tables: [deltas, endToEnd, anchor])
  |> group() |> sort(columns: ["hop", "_time"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["hop"], valueColumn: "_value") |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

defaults.noValue: No path: the path meter is off (smoking-pi enable pathmeter), it has not traced this target in the selected range, or the target has no ICMP series to tell hot from calm.
